keywords.name: Sustain Damage
keywords.text: Before hits are assigned, this unit can absorb one of them instead of being destroyed. Flip it face-down to show it is damaged; a damaged unit cannot sustain again until repaired, which happens automatically in the Status Phase.

keywords.name: Anti-Fighter Barrage
keywords.text: Rolled once at the start of space combat, before the first round. Hits from it can only destroy fighters, and they are not part of normal combat rounds — a ship with barrage still fires normally afterwards.

keywords.name: Bombardment
keywords.text: Fired from ships during invasion, before ground forces land. Each hit destroys one ground force on the planet. A planet with Planetary Shield cannot be bombarded at all.

keywords.name: Space Cannon
keywords.text: Fires in two places: Space Cannon Offense, when an enemy moves into the system, and Space Cannon Defense, against ground forces committed to the planet. Hits are assigned by the owner of the targeted units.

keywords.name: Planetary Shield
keywords.text: The planet cannot be targeted by Bombardment. It does not stop Space Cannon, and it does not prevent invasion — it only blocks orbital bombardment.

keywords.name: Production
keywords.text: Sets how many units the system can build during the Production step of a tactical action. Multiple producing units in one system add their values together.

keywords.name: Capacity
keywords.text: How many fighters and ground forces a ship can carry. Capacity across all ships in a system is pooled; exceeding it at the end of a move means the excess units are removed.

keywords.name: Combat
keywords.text: The number a die must meet or beat to score a hit. Lower is better. A notation like 7(x2) means the unit rolls two dice, each hitting on 7 or higher.

keywords.name: Move
keywords.text: How many systems the ship can travel through in one tactical action. Movement is blocked by systems containing enemy ships unless you have the relevant technology.

keywords.name: Cost
keywords.text: Resources needed to produce the unit. A notation like 1(x2) means the cost produces two of that unit at once — you cannot buy just one for half price.

strategyCards.name: Leadership
strategyCards.primary: Gain command tokens, and spend influence to gain more.
strategyCards.secondary: Spend influence to gain command tokens.

strategyCards.name: Diplomacy
strategyCards.primary: Choose a system and make it safe from other players' activation this round, then ready planets.
strategyCards.secondary: Spend a command token to ready planets.

strategyCards.name: Politics
strategyCards.primary: Choose a new speaker, draw action cards, and reorder the top of the agenda deck.
strategyCards.secondary: Spend a command token to draw action cards.

original.primary: Place one PDS or one space dock on a planet you control; then place one PDS on a planet you control.
original.secondary: Place a strategy token in any system, then place one PDS or one space dock on a planet you control in that system.

updated.primary: Either place one structure or use the Production ability of one of your space docks; then place one structure.
updated.secondary: Spend a strategy token to place one structure on a planet you control; the token is not placed on the board.

strategyCards.name: Trade
strategyCards.primary: Gain trade goods, replenish commodities, and let chosen players replenish theirs.
strategyCards.secondary: Spend a command token to replenish commodities.

original.primary: Remove one of your command tokens from the game board, gain one command token, then redistribute any number of tokens on your command sheet.
original.secondary: Spend a strategy token to use the Production ability of one of your space docks in your home system.

updated.primary: Perform a tactical action without placing a command token, even in a system that already has yours; you may redistribute command tokens before and after it.
updated.secondary: Spend a strategy token to use the Production abilities of units in your home system.

strategyCards.name: Technology
strategyCards.primary: Research a technology, then research a second by paying resources.
strategyCards.secondary: Spend a command token and resources to research one technology.

strategyCards.name: Imperial
strategyCards.primary: Score a public objective if you qualify, and gain a victory point for holding Mecatol Rex — otherwise draw a secret objective.
strategyCards.secondary: Spend a command token to draw a secret objective.

techColours.name: Propulsion
techColours.text: Movement, carrying capacity, and getting where others cannot.

techColours.name: Biotic
techColours.text: Ground forces, population, and card economy.

techColours.name: Cybernetic
techColours.text: Economy, production efficiency, and planet output.

techColours.name: Warfare
techColours.text: Combat strength, bombardment, and space cannon.

misunderstoodRules.question: What does my command token in a system actually lock?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Normally, you cannot activate a system that already contains your command token, and a ship cannot begin tactical-action movement in another system that contains your token. Your ships may move through your tokened systems, and another player's token does not lock you. Thunder's Edge Warfare can activate a system that already has your token, but it does not free ships that begin in a different tokened system.

misunderstoodRules.question: If activation places a token, how can ships move into the active system?
misunderstoodRules.answer: The movement restriction checks the systems where ships begin, not the token just placed in the destination. Place the tactic token to make a system active, then move eligible ships from systems that do not contain your command tokens into it.

misunderstoodRules.question: Do command tokens on the board return directly to my pools?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. During the Status Phase, board tokens are removed to your reinforcements. You then gain and redistribute command tokens as a separate step; removed board tokens do not automatically become usable pool tokens.

misunderstoodRules.question: What if an effect must place a token from reinforcements and none are there?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Take one of your choice from a pool on your command sheet and place it as instructed. This is different from gaining a token: if you must gain one and reinforcements are empty, you gain nothing.

misunderstoodRules.question: Can a player who passed still use strategy-card secondaries?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Yes. Passing ends that player's turns and actions for the phase, but they may still resolve other players' strategy-card secondary abilities.

misunderstoodRules.question: Can an Action ability be used whenever its owner wants?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. A component marked “Action:” is one of the actions you may take on your own turn during the Action Phase. Unless an effect grants an extra action, resolving it uses that turn's action.

misunderstoodRules.question: Does a canceled action card still count as played or as the turn's action?
misunderstoodRules.answer: The canceled card is discarded but is not treated as played, so another copy can be used in the same window if otherwise legal. If a component-action card is canceled, its action was not performed; the active player must take another action or pass if able. Sabotage cancels action cards, not heroes or other component abilities.

misunderstoodRules.question: Can I respond to any effect before it resolves?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Twilight Imperium has no general response stack. An ability can interrupt or follow an event only if its printed timing matches. Simultaneous Action Phase abilities resolve from the active player in initiative order; Strategy and Agenda Phase abilities begin with the Speaker and proceed clockwise.

misunderstoodRules.question: Does Production 5 mean five resources of units?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. It means up to five individual units. A fighter or infantry pair still counts as two units toward that limit, even though the pair has one combined cost. Production values from eligible units in the same system are added together.

misunderstoodRules.question: Can I split a fighter or infantry cost, or get change from planets?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. You may produce only one unit from a pair, but you still pay the pair's full cost. Add the total cost of everything being produced, then exhaust planets and spend trade goods to meet it; any excess value is lost.

misunderstoodRules.question: Does Sarween Tools apply whenever an effect says to produce units?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Only when at least one unit is using its named Production ability. An effect that merely says “produce” without using Production still requires payment, but Sarween Tools does not reduce that cost.

misunderstoodRules.question: For an objective requiring production in a system, do built units or their cost count?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. Count the printed Production values of your units in that system. The number or resource cost of units you happened to build is irrelevant.

misunderstoodRules.question: Do factions start with full commodities, and do commodities refill each round?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. Players start with zero commodities. They replenish only when an effect instructs them to, most commonly the Trade strategy card; round and phase changes do not replenish them by themselves.

misunderstoodRules.question: Can I flip my own commodities into trade goods?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Not by default. A commodity becomes a trade good when another player receives it. Your own commodities have no inherent spending value unless a specific effect says otherwise.

misunderstoodRules.question: Can one exhausted planet provide both resources and influence?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. Exhausting a planet spends either its resources or its influence for the current cost, never both. Trade goods may substitute one-for-one for resources or influence, except they cannot be used to cast Agenda Phase votes.

misunderstoodRules.question: What does 0 mean on the ten-sided die?
misunderstoodRules.answer: It is a 10, not zero. A roll of 0 therefore meets every ordinary combat or unit-ability threshold.

misunderstoodRules.question: When are fleet limits and capacity enforced?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Fleet pool is enforced immediately whenever non-fighter ships exceed the pool limit; remove excess ships at once. Fighters and ground forces ignore capacity during combat, then excess units are removed when combat ends. Capacity is also checked at other applicable times, including after movement.

misunderstoodRules.question: If a carrier is destroyed, do its fighters and infantry disappear immediately?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Not during combat. Capacity is pooled and fighters and ground forces remain through the fight. When space combat ends, remove any excess; that check occurs before invasion, so unsupported infantry cannot land afterward.

misunderstoodRules.question: Can combatants agree to skip rolls or ignore hits?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. Once combat is required, combat rolls and hit assignment are mandatory. Players can negotiate and use legal effects, but cannot replace the combat sequence with a private ceasefire.

misunderstoodRules.question: Does Anti-Fighter Barrage happen every combat round?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. It resolves only at the start of the first space-combat round, and its normal hits destroy fighters only. The step still occurs when no fighters are present because other abilities may trigger from its rolls or hits.

misunderstoodRules.question: Must I commit ground forces in order to bombard?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. Bombardment is resolved before ground forces are committed, so eligible ships may bombard even if you will land nothing. Planetary Shield still prevents bombardment unless an effect ignores it.

misunderstoodRules.question: Whom can Space Cannon Offense target?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Every player with an eligible unit may fire, but players other than the active player must target the active player's ships. If the active player fires, they choose a player with ships in the active system—normally the defender.

misunderstoodRules.question: Can adjacent PDS II units fire during Space Cannon Defense?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. The range increase used against ships does not extend Space Cannon Defense. Only eligible units on the invaded planet fire at ground forces committed to that same planet.

misunderstoodRules.question: Can ranged Space Cannon fire through wormholes?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Yes. Matching wormholes make their systems adjacent for all purposes, so an ability that reaches adjacent systems can use that adjacency unless another effect specifically says otherwise.

misunderstoodRules.question: Where can a normal retreat go, and when does it happen?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Announce it before rolling, survive that combat round, then move all eligible ships to one adjacent system containing one of your units or a planet you control and no other player's ships. Place a command token from reinforcements there unless yours is already present.

misunderstoodRules.question: Is Skilled Retreat treated as a retreat?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. It moves ships and ends the combat as printed, but rules and abilities that specifically refer to a retreat do not apply to it.

misunderstoodRules.question: Can the same player use more than one Direct Hit in a combat round?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Yes, if the cards affect different ships; the same-name restriction is about the same target in one timing window. Direct Hit normally works only after a ship uses Sustain Damage, so an ordinary mech on a planet is not a valid target.
misunderstoodRules.reference: LRR 2.6; Direct Hit errata and FAQ

misunderstoodRules.question: When does a gravity-rift ship roll, and how do multiple rifts work?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Merely entering a rift does not cause a roll. Roll immediately before each ship exits a rift it moved out of or through. Under the current Thunder's Edge clarification, each distinct rift can contribute its +1 movement once per ship. The Cabal's Crucible note adds one further +1 total and prevents those rolls for that movement.

misunderstoodRules.question: Does leaving a nebula make a ship's final move value exactly 1?
misunderstoodRules.answer: The ship treats its move value as 1 for that movement step, but modifiers such as Gravity Drive can still increase it.

misunderstoodRules.question: Can players transact during combat, and can a gift count as a transaction?
misunderstoodRules.answer: During the active player's turn, that player may transact once with each neighbor—even during combat. A transaction may be unequal or entirely one-sided, so giving something for nothing still counts as the transaction and can trigger abilities such as Pillage.

misunderstoodRules.question: When are transactions allowed outside the Action Phase?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Not while players are choosing strategy cards. During each agenda, every player may transact once with every other player, and they do not need to be neighbors. Otherwise, use the normal active-player-turn and neighbor rules unless an effect creates an exception.

misunderstoodRules.question: Does sitting next to someone at the table make us neighbors?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. Neighbor status comes from the map: the players share a system or have units or controlled planets in adjacent systems. Matching wormholes can create that adjacency.

misunderstoodRules.question: Can action cards be traded?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Normally no. Transactions exchange commodities, trade goods, promissory notes, and relic fragments. Action cards may be included only when the Emirates of Hacan is one of the two players in the transaction, due to their faction ability.

misunderstoodRules.question: Is a transaction limited to one promissory note total?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Each participant may give at most one promissory note from their hand, so a two-way transaction can contain one note in each direction. The limit is per transaction, not per round or for the entire game.

misunderstoodRules.question: Can a promissory note in a play area be traded again?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. Only notes in hand can be traded. Faceup notes placed in a play area, such as Support for the Throne or Alliance, remain there until their own text removes or returns them. Objectives that mention a note in your play area mean these faceup cards, not notes in hand.

misunderstoodRules.question: Must I use a promissory note when its timing occurs?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No, unless the note specifically makes its use mandatory. Also, a player cannot play their own color's or faction's promissory notes; those are bargaining tools for other players.

misunderstoodRules.question: Do resources or trade goods spent earlier in the round count toward a spend objective?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. Pay a spend objective's full listed cost when you score it, usually during the Score Objectives step. Earlier spending on units, technology, command tokens, or deals does not count.

misunderstoodRules.question: Can more than one player score the same public objective?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Yes. A public objective stays in the common area; every qualifying player can score it once. The game begins with two Stage I public objectives revealed.

misunderstoodRules.question: How many objectives can one player score?
misunderstoodRules.answer: During each Status Phase, at most one public and one status-phase secret. Action- and Agenda-Phase secrets use their printed timing; multiple may be scored in a turn or agenda phase, but only one during or after each combat. A player can hold at most three scored and unscored secret objectives combined.

misunderstoodRules.question: Does losing a home-system planet stop every kind of scoring?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. It prevents public-objective scoring. Secret objectives and victory points from other effects remain available unless their own requirements say otherwise. Imperial's scoring effect is for a public objective, not a secret one.

misunderstoodRules.question: What readies before and after the Agenda Phase?
misunderstoodRules.answer: The Status Phase readies all exhausted cards before the Agenda Phase begins, so planets used during the Action Phase are normally ready to vote. After both agendas, only planets ready again; exhausted technologies, agents, relics, and other cards wait for the next Status Phase unless another effect readies them.

misunderstoodRules.question: Can trade goods be spent as votes?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. Trade goods can substitute for influence costs, but casting votes is not spending influence. Votes normally come from exhausting planets for their influence or from effects that explicitly add votes.

misunderstoodRules.question: Can one player put multiple riders on the same agenda?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Yes, if they have different eligible cards or abilities. Resolve “after an agenda is revealed” abilities beginning with the Speaker and proceeding clockwise until everyone has used or declined the abilities they want. Each rider normally prevents its player from voting on that agenda, as printed on the card.

misunderstoodRules.question: Does Construction's secondary activate or lock the chosen system?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Using the original or Prophecy of Kings card places the spent strategy token in the chosen system; this does not perform an activation, but it does lock movement there. It can still be used if your token is already present, in which case the spent token returns to reinforcements. The revised Thunder's Edge card places no token on the board at all.

misunderstoodRules.question: How much can Warfare's secondary produce?
misunderstoodRules.answer: With the original card, one space dock in your home system uses Production; a second dock does not join it. With the revised Thunder's Edge card, all of your units with Production in your home system may contribute. In both versions, the spent strategy token is not placed in the home system.

misunderstoodRules.question: Can Scanlink explore a planet reached during the activation?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. Scanlink triggers when the system is activated, before movement. The chosen planet must already contain one or more of your units at that moment.

misunderstoodRules.question: What happens when an exploration deck runs out?
misunderstoodRules.answer: Shuffle that deck's discard pile to form a new deck. Purged cards are outside the game and do not return; discarded relic fragments and other discarded exploration cards do.

misunderstoodRules.question: Does using a legendary planet ability exhaust the planet too?
misunderstoodRules.answer: No. The legendary ability card and the planet card are separate components. Exhausting one does not exhaust the other unless the ability explicitly says so.

misunderstoodRules.question: How does L1Z1X Harrow work in a system with multiple invaded planets?
misunderstoodRules.answer: During the normal Bombardment step, assign each bombarding ship to one planet before rolling. Harrow is a separate bombardment after each ground-combat round; eligible ships in the system can bombard the planet where that ground combat occurred, regardless of which planet they targeted in the earlier Bombardment step.

thundersEdge.name: Thunder's Edge expedition
thundersEdge.text: At the end of a turn, a player may pay the cost of one unclaimed expedition slice and mark it with a control token. Their first claimed slice unlocks their faction's breakthrough. When all six slices are claimed, Thunder's Edge flips to its planet side and the final contributor places it in an eligible system; the player with the most claimed slices takes control and places that many infantry there.

thundersEdge.name: Breakthrough and synergy
thundersEdge.text: A breakthrough gives its faction a powerful ability and links two technology colors. For research requirements and technology-related objectives, a technology or specialty of either linked color may count as the other color, but a single component cannot count as both at once.

thundersEdge.name: The Fracture and ingress
thundersEdge.text: Whenever a breakthrough is gained and The Fracture is not already in play, that player rolls a die; a 1 or 10 brings it into play. Fracture systems are separate from the main galaxy and connect through ingress and egress tokens rather than ordinary tile borders.

thundersEdge.name: Neutral units
thundersEdge.text: Gray neutral units always fight a player sharing their space area. They use available unit abilities automatically, assign hits in the order defined by the expansion rules, and count as another player's units for effects even though there is no neutral player.

thundersEdge.name: Coexist
thundersEdge.text: Coexisting ground forces belonging to different players can remain on the same planet without beginning combat. The player whose units began coexisting does not take control, their structures are blockaded, and they count as controlling that planet only while checking objective requirements.

thundersEdge.name: Galvanized units
thundersEdge.text: A galvanized unit has a galvanize token beneath it and rolls one additional die whenever it makes a combat roll or resolves a unit ability roll.

thundersEdge.name: Galactic events
thundersEdge.text: A group may choose or randomly draw a galactic event during setup. Its rules modify the game for every player, and its complexity rating indicates how much the event changes normal play.

thundersEdge.name: Twilight's Fall
thundersEdge.text: This separate mode included with Thunder's Edge replaces normal factions with eight Mahact Kings. Players draft combinations of ability, unit-upgrade, and genome cards to build custom factions, and the mode uses its own strategy cards and components; its pieces are kept out of the site's standard-game faction and unit lists.

thundersEdge.name: Entropic scar
thundersEdge.text: Inside an entropic scar, printed unit abilities such as Sustain Damage, Production, Space Cannon, Bombardment, and Anti-Fighter Barrage cannot be used by or against units. At the start of the status phase, a player with ships there may spend a strategy token to gain one of their faction technologies.
